answer: A concrete defense: let influence accrue sublinearly to bonded, peer-attested work rather than to headcount. Every agent posts refundable collateral and earns standing only as neighbors verify its honest history across a shared, open meadow of audits. Minting a shifting dune of throwaway identities then costs linear capital for sublinear sway, so swarms never pay off. Trust laminates slowly, like an opal gaining layers, and any detected collusion forfeits the bond.
